title: Characteristics and Clinical Application of Extracellular Vesicle-Derived DNA
key_finding: This review reports that extracellular vesicle-derived DNA (EV DNA) offers higher stability and potentially greater sensitivity and specificity than cell-free DNA for biomarker detection in liquid biopsy, highlighting evidence of its utility across diagnostic and prognostic contexts, though specific quantitative metrics (e.g., exact sensitivity/specificity values or model performance) are not cons...

title: Extracellular Vesicle-Derived DNA vs. CfDNA as a Biomarker for the Detection of Colon Cancer
key_finding: The study found that extracellular vesicle-derived DNA (EV-DNA) and circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) have similar mutation detection sensitivity in colon cancer (EV-DNA: 61.9% vs cfDNA: 66.7%), with cfDNA yielding higher total DNA concentration and mutant-copy counts (p = 0.002 and p = 0.003), indicating no advantage of EV-DNA over cfDNA for mutation detection in this context.

title: Isolation of circulating exosomes and identification of exosomal PD-L1 for predicting immunotherapy response
key_finding: The SPR-ExoPD-L1 assay effectively isolates and detects exosomes from melanoma cells, providing valuable information for cancer diagnosis and personalized immunotherapy.

title: Exosomal PD-L1 detection in cancer predictive biomarker for response to immune checkpoint blockade therapy
key_finding: Exosomal PD-L1 detection shows potential as a non-invasive biomarker for predicting therapeutic response and monitoring disease progression in various cancer types.

title: Mechanisms underlying low-clinical responses to PD-1/PD-L1 blocking antibodies in immunotherapy of cancer: a key role of exosomal PD-L1
key_finding: Removal of exosomal PDL-1 may enhance the efficacy of anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in cancer patients by reducing resistance to these treatments.

title: Clinical Implications of Exosomal PD-L1 in Cancer Immunotherapy
key_finding: Exosomal PD-L1 plays a crucial role in tumor immune escape and resistance, and targeting it could advance cancer treatment.

title: Circulating extracellular vesicles expressing PD1 and PD-L1 predict response and mediate resistance to checkpoint inhibitors immunotherapy in metastatic melanoma
key_finding: Circulating PD1+ EVs are a key driver of resistance to anti-PD1 immunotherapy in metastatic melanoma patients, and liquid biopsy can effectively stratify them for immunotherapy.

title: Circulating exosomal immuno-oncological checkpoints and cytokines are potential biomarkers to monitor tumor response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in non-small cell lung cancer patients
key_finding: Exosomal immuno-oncological proteins/cytokines are potential biomarkers to monitor tumor response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy and predict clinical outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer patients.

title: Exosomal PD-L1 predicts response with immunotherapy in NSCLC patients
key_finding: Exosomal PD-L1 expression levels can predict the efficacy of immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer patients, providing a new tool for evaluating clinical efficacy of lung cancer immunotherapy.

title: Tracking the evolution of circulating exosomal-PD-L1 to monitor melanoma patients
key_finding: Circulating exosomal-PD-L1 levels are a more reliable marker for predicting tumor response to treatment and clinical outcome in melanoma patients than PD-L1 expression in tumor biopsies.

title: Small extracellular vesicle PD-L1 in cancer: the knowns and unknowns
key_finding: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) may be a promising diagnostic and prognostic marker for predicting clinical responses to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapies in cancer.

title: Homogeneous, Low-volume, Efficient, and Sensitive Quantitation of Circulating Exosomal PD-L1 for Cancer Diagnosis and Immunotherapy Response Prediction
key_finding: HOLMES-ExoPD-L1 is a more sensitive and efficient method for detecting circulating exosomal PD-L1 in cancer patients, potentially aiding in early diagnosis and immunotherapy response prediction.

title: Exosomal PD-L1: an effective liquid biopsy target to predict immunotherapy response
key_finding: Circulating exosomal PD-L1 levels reflect the state of anti-tumor immunity and can predict response to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, with higher pre-treatment exosomal PD-L1 associated with poorer response and dynamic changes during therapy correlating with treatment outcomes.

title: Validation of a multiomic model of plasma extracellular vesicle PD-L1 and radiomics for prediction of response to immunotherapy in NSCLC
key_finding: The study shows that a multiomic model combining plasma extracellular vesicle PD-L1 dynamics with radiomic imaging achieves high sensitivity and specificity in predicting non-response to immune-checkpoint inhibitors in NSCLC, outperforming tissue PD-L1 as a biomarker and correlating with tumor change.

title: PD-L1 on large extracellular vesicles is a predictive biomarker for therapy response in tissue PD-L1-low and -negative patients with non-small cell lung cancer
key_finding: In NSCLC patients with tissue PD-L1 low/negative, high baseline levels of PD-L1 on large extracellular vesicles (lEVs), particularly CD45−/CD62P+ platelet-derived vesicles, predict significantly better response to immunotherapy, establishing PD-L1+ lEVs as a quantitative biomarker for treatment response.

title: Exosomal biomarkers and immune checkpoint inhibitors: advancements and future prospects
key_finding: The paper reviews evidence that exosomal PD-L1 levels and cargo can reflect dynamic tumor-immune changes and may predict immunotherapy response and monitor treatment, but it does not present a single new quantitative result; it highlights promising correlations and the need for standardized quantitative thresholds to reliably predict response.

title: The role of exosomal PD-L1 in tumor progression and immunotherapy
key_finding: Exosomal PD-L1 levels correlate with response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy and may reflect treatment monitoring needs, with higher exosomal PD-L1 associated with greater immune suppression and potential resistance, suggesting exosomal PD-L1 as a quantitative biomarker for predicting and tracking immunotherapy outcomes.

title: Monitoring of single extracellular vesicle heterogeneity in cancer progression and therapy
key_finding: Single extracellular vesicles (EVs) show complex molecular diversity, affecting cancer progression and immune modulation, offering potential for non-invasive diagnostic approaches using liquid biopsy.

title: Extracellular vesicle heterogeneity through the lens of multiomics
key_finding: Multiomics can reveal the molecular cargo of large oncosomes, which may help stratify patients and serve as prognostic markers in liquid biopsy.

title: Single Extracellular VEsicle Nanoscopy
key_finding: SEVEN is a robust and effective method for analyzing extracellular vesicle subpopulations in human plasma, revealing unique pancreatic cancer-enriched EV subpopulations.

title: Analysis of single extracellular vesicles for biomedical applications with especial emphasis on cancer investigations
key_finding: This paper highlights advances in single extracellular vesicle analysis and detection for biomedical applications, particularly cancer investigations, highlighting the need for comprehensive characterization and sensitive detection.

title: Current Advances in Technologies for Single Extracellular Vesicle Analysis and Its Clinical Applications in Cancer Diagnosis
key_finding: Advances in single extracellular vesicle analysis technologies may enable precise study of EV heterogeneity and cargo, potentially benefiting cancer early diagnosis.

title: Harnessing extracellular vesicle heterogeneity for diagnostic and therapeutic applications
key_finding: EV heterogeneity can be exploited for diagnostic and therapeutic applications in cancer detection, wound healing, and neurodegenerative and cardiovascular diseases, but requires modern analytical platforms with single-particle resolution.

title: Single Extracellular Vesicle Imaging and Computational Analysis Identifies Inherent Architectural Heterogeneity
key_finding: Cryogenic transmission electron microscopy reveals consistent architectural heterogeneity in extracellular vesicles, offering insights into their complex actions and biodistribution.

title: Microfluidic Platform for Profiling of Extracellular Vesicles from Single Breast Cancer Cells
key_finding: This study demonstrates that single breast cancer cells secrete enough extracellular vesicles to extract their tissue fingerprint, highlighting their potential as diagnostic markers and enabling fundamental studies of vesicle biogenesis.

title: Colocalization of protein and microRNA markers reveals unique extracellular vesicle subpopulations for early cancer detection
key_finding: The NOBEL-SPA technique reveals unique extracellular vesicle subpopulations that can detect early-stage breast cancer, offering potential for clinical examination and therapeutics development.

title: Extracellular Vesicles in Cancer: Mechanistic Insights and Clinical Applications
key_finding: The paper is a narrative review and does not report a specific quantitative finding on single extracellular vesicle analysis or EV heterogeneity in cancer. It summarizes mechanistic roles, biogenesis, isolation methods, and potential clinical applications of extracellular vesicles in cancer, including techniques used for EV isolation and their cargo (miRNAs, proteins) related to tumor biology and...

title: Toward Clarity in Single Extracellular Vesicle Research: Defining the Field and Correcting Missteps
key_finding: This perspective argues for a precise, standardized definition of single EV research to reveal and quantify EV heterogeneity, but it does not present a new quantitative experimental finding; instead, it calls for rigorous, multimodal characterization to accurately assess single EV properties relevant to cancer diagnostics and therapeutics.

title: Extracellular vesicles in cancer´s communication: messages we can read and how to answer | Molecular Cancer | Springer Nature Link
key_finding: The paper is a review and does not present original quantitative data on single extracellular vesicle analysis or quantitative heterogeneity in cancer; it synthesizes current knowledge on EV biogenesis, cargo, and their roles in tumor progression and as biomarkers, without reporting a specific numerical metric for single-vesicle heterogeneity.

title: Single-vesicle heterogeneity and uptake of extracellular vesicles affected by oncogenic KRAS and BRAF revealed by proteomics and nano-flow cytometry
key_finding: Mutant KRAS- and BRAF-derived extracellular vesicles show heightened uptake and altered trafficking with increased levels of CD44, LSR, ITGB4, and CSPG4, enabling more efficient nuclear delivery of payloads (e.g., doxorubicin) compared to wild-type EVs.

title: Single Extracellular VEsicle Nanoscopy-Universal Protocol (SEVEN-UP): Accessible Imaging Platform for Quantitative Characterization of Single Extracellular Vesicles
key_finding: The SEVEN-UP study introduces a universal, affordable protocol using SRRF-based single-EV imaging to quantify, on a per-vesicle basis, number, size, and cargo content, demonstrating that RNA-containing EVs from HEK 293T cells are on average larger (and represent ~18% of EVs) than RNA-free EVs, highlighting pronounced heterogeneity in single-EV composition relevant to cancer biomarker analysis.

title: Exosome removal as a therapeutic adjuvant in cancer
key_finding: Extracorporeal hemofiltration using the Aethlon ADAPTTM system could improve immune dysfunction and response to standard cancer treatments by targeting immune suppressive exosomes.

title: Abstract 4509: Targeting tumor-derived exosomes using a lectin affinity hemofiltration device
key_finding: The Hemopurifier effectively clears exosomes from plasma from diverse cancer types, exhibiting malignancy and immunosuppressive signatures.

title: Modification of immune cell-derived exosomes for enhanced cancer immunotherapy: current advances and therapeutic applications
key_finding: Modified immune cell-derived exosomes show potential for enhanced cancer immunotherapy by improving drug delivery efficiency and antitumor effects.

title: Targeted inhibition of tumor-derived exosomes as a novel therapeutic option for cancer
key_finding: Targeted inhibition of tumor-derived exosomes may improve cancer treatment and prognosis by regulating tumor development and progression, contributing to drug resistance, and enhancing antitumor immune response.

title: Tumor-Derived Exosomes in Tumor-Induced Immune Suppression
key_finding: Tumor-derived exosomes (TEX) contribute to immune suppression by activating suppressive pathways in immune cells, and targeting them may offer potential for immunotherapy.

title: A Pro-Metastatic Derivatives Eliminator for In Vivo Dual-Removal of Circulating Tumor Cells and Tumor-Derived Exosomes Impedes their Biodistribution into Distant Organs
key_finding: The PMDE device effectively removes circulating tumor cells and tumor-derived exosomes from peripheral blood, inhibiting their biodistribution into distant organs, potentially preventing cancer recurrence and metastasis.

title: The avatar principle: exosomal dynamics guiding tumor adaptation and next-generation therapeutic strategies
key_finding: Exosomes can be used as avatars of strategy, undermining host defenses while redirecting immunity against tumors, offering new horizons for precision cancer immunotherapy.

title: Curvature-sensing peptide inhibits tumour-derived exosomes for enhanced cancer immunotherapy
key_finding: A curvature-sensing peptide can enhance cancer immunotherapy by disrupting tumor-derived exosomes, improving treatment outcomes in tumor-bearing mice.

title: Enhancing Chemotherapy-Related Immune Responses via Bioorthogonal Metabolic Engineering-Driven Tumor Exosomes Elimination
key_finding: The Biordee strategy effectively reduces tumor cell-driven exosomes in the circulatory system, enhancing immune response after chemotherapy and inhibiting breast cancer liver metastases.

title: Dendritic Cell-Derived Exosomes in Cancer Immunotherapy
key_finding: Dendritic cell-derived exosomes (DEXs) show potential in promoting immune cell-dependent tumor rejection and avoiding tumor cell-mediated immunosuppression in cancer immunotherapy.

title: Hemopurifier device in patients with solid tumours who have stable or progressive disease while on a treatment that includes pembrolizumab or nivolumab: protocol for an Australian safety, feasibility and dose-finding study
key_finding: The paper protocol posits that using the Hemopurifier hemofiltration device to remove tumor-derived extracellular vesicles in patients on anti-PD-1 therapy is safe and feasible across three dose cohorts, with data collection on adverse events, EV concentrations, and immune/tumor responses to identify a dose that reduces EVs and potentially enhances anti-tumor T cell activity.

title: Protocol for a Safety, Feasibility, and Dose-Finding Study of the Hemopurifier® Device in Patients with Solid Tumors Who Have Stable or Progressive Disease During Pembrolizumab or Nivolumab Monotherapy
key_finding: The paper reports a 3+3 safety/feasibility dose-finding design for the Hemopurifier, with three treatment cohorts (one, two, or three sessions over one week) to assess safety, kinetics of extracellular vesicle (EV) removal, and rebound, though no final efficacy data or quantitative exosome removal metrics are provided in this preprint excerpt.

title: Exosomes as a tumor immune escape mechanism: possible therapeutic implications
key_finding: The paper reports that extracorporeal removal of tumor-derived exosomes using hollow-fiber filtration can reduce circulating exosome levels and potentially alleviate cancer-associated immunosuppression, suggesting a measurable therapeutic effect through exosome scavenging/hemofiltration (quantitative data on reductions would be in the study’s experiments).

title: Plasma Exchange May Enhance Antitumor Effects by Removal of Soluble Programmed Death-Ligand 1 and Extracellular Vesicles: Preliminary Study
key_finding: Therapeutic plasma exchange with extracellular vesicle filtration reduced tumor-derived EVs by about 75% in vitro, and when combined with T-DM1, it produced earlier tumor shrinkage in a rat model, suggesting plasma exchange–mediated removal of soluble PD-L1 and EVs can enhance ADC antitumor efficacy and counteract immunosuppression.

title: Tumor-derived exosomes in cancer progression and treatment failure
key_finding: The paper reviews that tumor-derived exosomes contribute to cancer progression and treatment failure by carrying molecules that modulate immune responses and therapeutic efficacy, implying that strategies like removal or scavenging of exosomes could potentially improve cancer therapy, though the article itself does not provide a specific numerical value for such effects.
